nodes.label: Authoring tools
nodes.summary: What Claude works with: the skill says how to write a guide, and the CLI checks each patch against the code. CLI drafts give the boxes and steps, and Claude writes the text.

nodes.label: Skill
nodes.summary: The steps Claude follows to make a guide: when to draft, how to write, and worked patches. `xpl skill install` copies the skill to your agent and points its `bin/xpl` launcher at the installed CLI.

nodes.label: CLI
nodes.summary: The `xpl` command that Claude and you run. The CLI builds the index, checks and applies patches, reports what still needs work and writes the guide page.
nodes.detail: The build writes the npm package `@krimvp/xpl` (MIT) to `packages/cli/dist`: the CLI, the viewer page, the grammars and the skill. Besides that path, the CLI serves a local page (`xpl view`), records requests from that page (`xpl feedback`, `xpl revise`) and prepares guides for pull requests (`xpl stage`, `xpl pr`). `xpl --help` lists every command.

nodes.label: Indexer
nodes.summary: Reads the source files and records each function, class and config key with its lines and a hash, plus the references between them. Each reference is `precise` (from a SCIP tool) or `heuristic` (matched by name).
nodes.detail: Language packs cover TypeScript and JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, YAML, JSON and TOML; Rust, Ruby and PHP get declarations from tags. The SCIP tools are scip-typescript, scip-python and scip-go. `xpl index` writes `.explainer/index-<commit>.json`, which git ignores.

nodes.label: Core rules
nodes.summary: The shared rules, with no file or network access: the guide format, code links, patch merging, checks and the arrows of a map. The CLI and the viewer both use core, so both check a claim the same way.

nodes.label: Viewer
nodes.summary: The page you read: diagrams next to the code, linked both ways. `xpl bundle` puts the guide, the index and the source files inside this one HTML file.
nodes.detail: The page has four tabs (Tour, Map, Flow and Code) and a Present mode for a talk. Under `xpl view` the page talks to a local server. You can then edit the text, ask for an explanation and save.

nodes.label: build-index.ts
nodes.summary: The index command selects precision and commit options, builds the index and writes it. Its summary reports reference coverage per language.

nodes.label: build.ts
nodes.summary: The builder captures source snapshots and runs syntax and semantic providers. Shared normalization checks source evidence before coverage controls merging.

nodes.label: files.ts
nodes.summary: Discovery uses git or a directory walk, then filters generated artifacts, binaries and oversized files. File extensions select language packs.

nodes.label: commit.ts
nodes.summary: An explicit commit option names the index when provided. Otherwise a clean repository uses HEAD; other trees use a content-based identifier.

nodes.label: parse.ts
nodes.summary: A parser pool reuses one tree-sitter parser per grammar. Each parsed file carries its context and language pack until disposal.

nodes.label: types.ts
nodes.summary: The language-pack contract describes extraction, site classification and module resolution. Packs return facts; the framework supplies ids, hashes and resolved references.

nodes.label: typescript.ts
nodes.summary: The TypeScript pack extracts symbols, imports and reference sites. The pack also classifies sites and resolves module paths for TypeScript and JavaScript.

nodes.label: hash.ts
nodes.summary: `FileHasher` hashes complete line ranges using Node SHA-256, preserving indentation and blank lines. Its versioned hashes match core `hashText`, with a checked fallback if the algorithms differ.

nodes.label: symbols.ts
nodes.summary: Symbol assembly assigns ids, duplicate suffixes, ranges, hashes and parents. Position lookup supplies the enclosing symbol for a reference site.

nodes.label: heuristic.ts
nodes.summary: The heuristic resolver follows scopes, imports and declared types. Function values remain reads; unresolved sites are omitted rather than invented.

nodes.label: resolvers.ts
nodes.summary: Each SCIP resolver runs its pinned language tool and maps the output onto indexed symbols. The resolver reports coverage alongside references.

nodes.label: run.ts
nodes.summary: Pinned SCIP tools run in temporary directories with a timeout. The runner decodes their output and reports tool failures.

nodes.label: map.ts
nodes.summary: The SCIP mapper links occurrences to indexed definitions and asks the language pack to classify each site. The mapper also reports described files.

nodes.label: typescriptPack
nodes.summary: The pack serves TypeScript, TSX and JavaScript with file-scoped names. Its extraction facts feed heuristic resolution and precise-site classification.

nodes.label: cli.ts
nodes.summary: Dispatch looks up a command and awaits its handler. The entry point formats errors and returns the command’s exit code.

nodes.label: commands/apply.ts
nodes.summary: The apply handler reads and validates a patch before writing accepted changes. Rejected or wholly protected changes return exit code one.

nodes.label: repo.ts
nodes.summary: Workspace loading chooses an index and provides cached source text. Strict validation and export require that index to match the working tree.

nodes.label: fsutil.ts
nodes.summary: File helpers provide atomic writes, JSON parsing and source readers. Parse errors identify the offending input when possible.

nodes.label: format.ts
nodes.summary: Text formatting for command output: `renderIssue` prints one issue as `severity path [element id]: message`, `issueSummary` counts errors and warnings.

nodes.label: core/apply.ts
nodes.summary: The applier checks fields, merges by id, constructs anchors and validates a cloned explainer. User-owned fields are preserved for the LLM actor.

nodes.label: validate.ts
nodes.summary: Checks a whole explainer against the index and the current code: ids, references, ownership and code links. In strict mode a drifted or missing link is an error, and the message says when only the user can repair it.

nodes.label: anchors.ts
nodes.summary: Builds code links and checks them again later. `makeAnchor` stores a range and a hash of its lines, and `resolveWith` checks one link again as ok, moved, drifted or missing.

nodes.label: text.ts
nodes.summary: Source hashes keep whitespace as it is and read CRLF as LF, using `sha256-v2:` plus 12 SHA-256 hex digits. `normalizeLines` remains a text-matching helper; it must not be used to hash source evidence.

nodes.label: index-model.ts
nodes.summary: The index model supplies file, symbol and reference lookups. Suggestions help repair unresolved names without silently retargeting anchors.

nodes.label: applyCommand.run
nodes.summary: The command selects an actor, loads inputs and applies the patch. The command writes accepted changes unless dry-run was requested.

nodes.label: Applier
nodes.summary: One applier manages each patch’s cloned result, issues and changed ids. Actor-specific ownership checks protect user edits during merging.

nodes.label: main.tsx
nodes.summary: The page loads its embedded bundle, creates the store and renders the app. Missing or malformed data produces opening guidance.

nodes.label: store.ts
nodes.summary: The store manages navigation, editing and source caches. Live polling refreshes explanation, source and index data while preserving unsaved edits.

nodes.label: derive.ts
nodes.summary: Memoized derivation computes diagrams, selected code ranges, editor panes and caret matches. Unchanged inputs reuse previous results.

nodes.label: hooks.ts
nodes.summary: React bindings for the store: useStore returns it, useViewerState subscribes to it with useSyncExternalStore, and useDerived returns getDerived of the current state.

nodes.label: DiagramPane.tsx
nodes.summary: The pane renders the selected diagram under its title and question. Graph views also expose their available exploration controls.

nodes.label: GraphView.tsx
nodes.summary: Draws a laid-out map as SVG, with a `data-element-id` on each box and arrow. A click selects that element in the store, and state classes mark what is selected, matched or related.

nodes.label: SequenceView.tsx
nodes.summary: The sequence renderer draws lifelines, frames and message rows. Selection, matches and related elements have visual states.

nodes.label: graphLayout.ts
nodes.summary: Places the boxes and routes the arrows of a map, inside each container before its parent. Boxes the user pinned keep their place, and the other boxes make room for them.

nodes.label: EditorStack.tsx
nodes.summary: The stack creates a source editor per derived pane. Focus, scrolling and caret state connect those editors to the store.

nodes.label: editor.ts
nodes.summary: Editor setup supplies syntax coloring and read-only source views. The editor applies focus decorations and reports selected line ranges.

nodes.label: focus.ts
nodes.summary: Focus collects each element’s source ranges and combines them by file. Reverse lookup finds elements covering a source line.

nodes.label: graph.ts
nodes.summary: Graph derivation combines indexed references with authored overlays and view filters. Pure helpers also support expanding and collapsing boxes.

nodes.label: stubs.ts
nodes.summary: Stub planning represents references crossing a view’s boundary. The stub builder ranks nearby ghosts and folds excess neighbors into readable groups.

nodes.label: loadBundle
nodes.summary: The loader parses the embedded data script through core. The loader returns a bundle or an actionable error without throwing.

nodes.label: parseBundle
nodes.summary: JSON-parses the text of the bundle script and throws unless its `schema` is `code-explainer/bundle@0`.

nodes.label: ViewerStore
nodes.summary: Store actions update navigation, source and author edits, then notify subscribers. Live workspace refresh rebuilds the model against its current index.

nodes.label: DiagramPane
nodes.summary: The component selects a renderer using the current view. The pane passes selection, caret matches and related ids to that renderer.

nodes.label: deriveGraph
nodes.summary: References are lifted to the boxes representing their endpoints. Stored overlays, hidden elements and stub policy shape the resulting graph.

nodes.label: GraphView
nodes.summary: The graph renderer fits layout to its pane and draws an interactive SVG. Empty, pending and failed layouts have explicit states.

nodes.label: SequenceView
nodes.summary: The component lays out participants, frames and messages as a sequence diagram. Its elements remain linked to the model and selection.

nodes.label: EditorPane
nodes.summary: A pane creates its editor when source is available. The pane applies focus and caret state and reports changes back to the store.

nodes.label: resolveCommand.run
nodes.summary: Runs `xpl resolve`: checks the code links again with `reresolveExplainer` and prints the report. With `--write` the command saves the result, and it refuses an index older than the files unless you pass `--allow-stale`.

nodes.label: reresolveExplainer
nodes.summary: Checks the code links of a copy of the explainer again and binds the copy to the new index. Returns the copy with a report: counts per status, drifted elements by owner and missing links.

nodes.label: resolveWith
nodes.summary: Anchor resolution checks current source against the stored hash. The resolver distinguishes unchanged, moved, drifted and missing locations.

nodes.label: searchSpan
nodes.summary: Looks for the stored hash in windows of the original length, nearest to the expected start first. Unchanged text that moved is found this way; indentation or blank lines inserted inside the span cause drift.

nodes.label: IndexModel
nodes.summary: The in-memory model of an index: lookups of files and symbols by path, and suggestions of similar files (`suggestFiles`) and symbols (`suggestSymbols`).

nodes.label: statusCommand.run
nodes.summary: Status lists missing explanations, drift, broken references and queued requests. User-owned drift is reported separately for manual review.

nodes.label: applyPatch
nodes.summary: Merges a patch into an explainer: it builds an `Applier` for the actor and runs the patch through it.

nodes.label: makeAnchor
nodes.summary: Anchor construction resolves the target and hashes its current source. The builder rejects ambiguous text, invalid spans, unavailable files and stale evidence.

nodes.label: providers.ts
nodes.summary: Independent providers return declarations, evidenced relationships and analysis reports. xpl normalizes source positions, assigns canonical IDs and merges only covered capabilities and files.

nodes.label: tree-sitter.ts
nodes.summary: The syntax provider extracts plain declarations and resolves heuristic relationships. Its optional classifier keeps parsing behind the provider seam.

nodes.label: repo.ts
nodes.summary: SourceRepoView caches repository text and directory membership for module resolution.

nodes.label: You
nodes.summary: Asks a question about the code, reads the guide and checks that its text is true.

nodes.label: Claude
nodes.summary: Reads the code and writes the guide's text as patches, by the steps of the code-explainer skill.

nodes.label: Your repository
nodes.summary: The code that the guide explains. xpl reads its files, and for a change also its git history.

nodes.label: Guide files
nodes.summary: Keeps each guide as `.explainer/<name>.explainer.json`, which you commit, next to the index of the code, which git ignores.

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.summary: Shows the guide: one HTML file that opens without a server, or a local page that `xpl view` serves.

nodes.label: xpl
nodes.summary: Checks the code links of a guide against your code, and builds the page that shows the guide.

edges.label: bin/xpl runs dist/xpl.mjs
edges.summary: The skill launcher reads its installed CLI binding or the development build. The launcher warns about a version mismatch, then imports the CLI in the same process.

edges.label: viewer page (dist/index.html)
edges.summary: The CLI reads the built viewer page and injects explanation data. Both offline export and the live server use that page.

edges.label: HTTP /api (xpl view)
edges.summary: The local API loads source and saves authored edits and feedback. Managed requests carry the loaded repository and guide; an address serving another attachment is refused.

edges.label: applyPatch, injectBundle, …
edges.summary: CLI handlers use core for explanation creation, patch checking and bundle injection. The CLI supplies the surrounding file access.

edges.label: buildIndex, writeIndex, …
edges.summary: `xpl index` calls `buildIndex` and saves the result with `writeIndex`, which replaces the old index file in one step. `--scip` imports a SCIP file made beforehand, and `--no-cache` extracts every file again.

edges.label: hashText, splitLines, …
edges.summary: The indexer follows core’s source-hash rules. Its native hashing implementation checks compatibility before using the faster path.

edges.label: parseBundle, deriveGraph, …
edges.summary: The viewer uses core to parse bundles and derive displayed graphs. Packed indexes are unpacked during loading.

edges.label: pack.extract(ctx)
edges.summary: On a cache miss, the syntax adapter asks the language pack for plain declarations and relationship sites. The adapter frees the tree before storing facts.

edges.label: pack.resolveModule(spec, file, repo)
edges.summary: Module resolution dispatches through the importing file’s language pack. Its callback assignment links the resolver to a language-specific implementation.

edges.label: pack.classifySite(ctx, line, col)
edges.summary: The syntax adapter classifies source positions and returns plain sites. SCIP consumes those facts through an optional callback.

edges.label: provider.analyze(input)
edges.summary: Index construction runs semantic providers on every build. Their source-backed facts share normalization and a merge controlled by observed coverage.

edges.label: command.run(ctx, args)
edges.summary: Command dispatch invokes the registered handler with parsed arguments. The CLI awaits the handler and reports its outcome.

edges.label: throw CliError, then `error: ...`
edges.summary: Malformed patch JSON raises a CLI error before merging. The entry point formats the error and returns a failure code.

edges.label: applyPatch(...)
edges.summary: `run` passes the explainer, the patch, the index model, the working-tree text cache and the actor to `applyPatch`.

edges.label: loadExplainer / openWorkspace
edges.summary: The locked apply helper loads the latest explainer; the command opens its workspace and gives the model and texts to applyPatch.

edges.label: parseJson / atomicWrite
edges.summary: readPatch parses JSON, and the locked apply helper serializes and atomically publishes accepted content.

edges.label: renderIssues / issueSummary
edges.summary: `run` prints every issue with `renderIssues` (one `severity path [id]: message` line each) and heads the issue list of a successful apply with `issueSummary` (`N errors, M warnings`).

edges.label: workingTreeReader / parseJson
edges.summary: `WorkingTree` reads files through `workingTreeReader`, and `readExplainerFile` parses the explainer file with `parseJson`.

edges.label: new TextCache(...)
edges.summary: `WorkingTree` builds a `TextCache` over the working-tree reader and a `git show` reader for the code before a change. `openWorkspace` returns it as `texts`, the cache `run` passes to `applyPatch`.

edges.label: makeAnchor(...)
edges.summary: `Applier.anchors` builds each stored anchor with `makeAnchor`. `anchorOptions` gives it hints from the explainer's own whole-symbol anchors (`storedSymbolHints`) for its `Did you mean` candidates, and the change record for base anchors.

edges.label: validateExplainer(...)
edges.summary: `Applier.validate` runs `validateExplainer` in strict mode on the caller's explainer and on the merged copy.

edges.label: resolveWith(...)
edges.summary: `checkAnchors` calls `resolveWith` for each stored anchor to learn whether it is ok, moved, drifted or missing.

edges.label: normalizeLines / hashText
edges.summary: Blank-span checks normalize lines for emptiness. Source hashes preserve indentation and blank lines when checking evidence.

edges.label: file / symbolAt / suggestSymbols
edges.summary: `makeAnchor` looks the file and symbol up in the index and, when one is not there, asks `suggestFiles` or `suggestSymbols` for the `Did you mean` candidates.

edges.label: state changed
edges.summary: State replacement notifies store subscribers. React hooks subscribe to those notifications and render the updated workspace.

edges.label: onCursor(from, to)
edges.summary: `createReadOnlyEditor` installs a listener that calls `handlers.onCursor` with the selected lines, and `EditorPane` forwards them to `store.setCursor` except in a "before" pane. The handler is a stored function, so the index has no call arrow from editor.ts to EditorStack.tsx.

edges.label: resolveWith
edges.summary: Validation resolves anchors against current source. Strict mode rejects drifted or missing locations; lenient mode reports repair warnings.

edges.label: makeAnchor
edges.summary: Unprotected patch anchors are built from current code. Stale evidence fails; successful construction supplies a current hash and resolved range.

edges.label: validateExplainer
edges.summary: Patch validation checks the merged explanation. Introduced or touched errors reject it, while unrelated existing errors become repair warnings.

edges.label: getDerived
edges.summary: useDerived returns getDerived of the current state, so the components that call it read the same memoised Derived for one state.

edges.label: deriveGraph, repr
edges.summary: Graph views use core derivation for their boxes and edges. Representation lookup also connects stubs and related elements to those boxes.

edges.label: codeFocus, reverse index
edges.summary: For a click, derive.ts calls `codeFocus` and `mergeFocusByFile`. For the cursor, `viewReverseIndex` calls `viewCandidates` once per view and builds one reverse index for drawn elements and one for concepts.

edges.label: deriveGraph, derivedEdgeAnchors, viaAnchors
edges.summary: `viewCandidates` derives the view's graph when the caller passes none. `derivedFocus` and `focusOf` get the code ranges of a derived arrow, or of the hops of a `via` arrow, from graph.ts.

edges.label: planStubs
edges.summary: deriveGraph reads the view's stub policy with resolveStubPolicy and hands the stub candidates it collected to planStubs, which decides which ghosts and stubs are drawn.

edges.label: expandStub, drillIn, collapse
edges.summary: View actions apply pure graph helpers and retain the resulting include list. Expanding or collapsing changes which code is represented.

edges.label: GraphView
edges.summary: For a graph view DiagramPane passes the derived graph, stored coordinate pins, selection, caret matches and related IDs to GraphView. Pinned graph load and Fit keep zoom at least 0.9; larger maps pan at readable label size.

edges.label: SequenceView
edges.summary: The pane supplies the sequence view and model to its renderer. Sequence layout follows participants and messages rather than graph derivation.

edges.label: layoutGraphFitting
edges.summary: GraphView passes stored pins or a local drag preview to layoutGraphFitting. BoxShape uses badgeWidth for its badge.

edges.label: click, drillIn, expandStub
edges.summary: Diagram interactions select elements, drill into boxes or expand stubs. Those actions update the store and its source focus.

edges.label: click
edges.summary: A click on a step or a lifeline calls store.click, and a click on the empty canvas calls clearSelection.

edges.label: createReadOnlyEditor, applyFocus
edges.summary: A source pane creates a read-only editor and applies range decorations. Scrolling follows the range most relevant to the current step.

edges.label: setCursor, ensureFile
edges.summary: Caret changes update reverse lookup through the store. Missing source is fetched from the live API when available.

edges.label: asks a question
edges.summary: You name the question and the reader; the skill turns that into a guide.

edges.label: sends patches
edges.summary: Claude runs the `xpl` commands and sends its text as JSON patches; `xpl apply` checks each one before it saves.

edges.label: reads the code
edges.summary: `xpl index` lists the files and records their symbols, lines and hashes.

edges.label: saves the guide
edges.summary: Only `xpl apply` and `xpl change` write the guide file, and only after a patch passes every check.

edges.label: builds the page
edges.summary: `xpl bundle` puts the guide, the index and the code into the viewer page, which the browser opens.

edges.label: reads the guide
edges.summary: You click a box to see its code, or put the cursor in the code to see the boxes about it.

concepts.label: Code links
concepts.summary: A code link, stored as an anchor, points a claim at a file, a symbol or lines inside it. The link keeps a hash of those lines, and xpl marks it ok, moved, drifted or missing when the code changes.
concepts.detail: A link can name a whole file, a symbol, a line span or a unique piece of text (`find`). The checks prove that the code is there and unchanged, not that the text about it is true.

anchors.symbol: text.hashes preserve indentation and blank lines, canonicalizing CRLF only
resolveAnchor: whole symbols and files.is drifted when the symbol text changed

concepts.label: The user's edits win
concepts.summary: Each element records who wrote it and which fields the user edited. A patch from Claude never changes those, and `xpl apply` reports each item it skipped.
concepts.detail: Edits saved in the viewer count as the user's. A patch that only touches protected items applies nothing and exits 1.

anchors.symbol: applyPatch: user protection.an llm patch never modifies a user-authored element (skipped with a warning)
applyPatch: user protection.an llm patch keeps the fields listed in userFields and updates the rest

concepts.label: Precise and heuristic references
concepts.summary: A reference from a SCIP tool is `precise`. Where no tool ran, or the tool skipped a file, xpl's own match by name stays, labelled `heuristic`, and the viewer draws those arrows lighter.
concepts.detail: In `auto` mode a failed tool prints a warning and the heuristic references stay. In `require` mode the build fails instead. An arrow that holds both kinds keeps the lighter style.

anchors.symbol: precise references replace heuristic ones per file.heuristic references of described files are replaced (dropped when the tool has none), those of other files stay
deriveGraph: derived edges.keeps uniform reference resolution

concepts.label: Arrows are worked out
concepts.summary: The map draws an arrow between two boxes when the index has references between their code, and nobody stores those arrows. Claude's text adds labels and meaning on top of them.

anchors.symbol: deriveGraph: derived edges.aggregates references per (kind, from, to) with count, resolution and anchors
deriveGraph: stored edges.overlays a stored edge on the derived edge with the same id (no duplicate)

concepts.label: All or nothing
concepts.summary: A rejected patch writes nothing: `xpl apply` lists every problem at once and exits 1. The guide file on disk stays as it was until the patch is clean.
concepts.detail: Core merges the patch into a copy before it checks anything. The CLI writes the file only for an accepted result with changes, and `--dry-run` checks without writing.

anchors.symbol: applyPatch: atomicity and validation.applies nothing when any element fails
applyPatch: atomicity and validation.pre-existing problems elsewhere.does not block a patch on untouched elements (drifted anchors of user concepts, etc_)
applyPatch: atomicity and validation.pre-existing problems elsewhere.still rejects a patch that makes things worse
xpl apply.rejects a bad symbol, prints the suggestion and path, and writes nothing

views.title: The four packages and the skill inside xpl

scope.question: What are the parts of xpl and how do they depend on each other?

views.title: From a repository to a page, command by command

scope.question: What happens, command by command, from indexing a repository to the viewer showing an explainer?

steps.label: xpl index: buildIndex({ root, precise, cache, commit })
steps.summary: `xpl index` reads every source file and writes the index of symbols and references to `.explainer/`. A second run reuses what it found in files that did not change, and resolves every reference again.

steps.label: xpl new: createExplainer({ title, repoName, index, indexPath })
steps.summary: `xpl new` creates an empty explainer and binds it to the chosen index. The repository's metadata gives its first name.

steps.label: xpl apply: applyPatch(explainer, patch, index, texts, { actor })
steps.summary: `xpl apply` checks a patch against the code and the ownership rules before it writes. An accepted patch updates the explainer file.

steps.label: xpl bundle: injectBundle(html, bundle)
steps.summary: `xpl bundle` runs the ready check, then writes one HTML file with the guide, the code it shows and a packed index. A failed check stops the command, and `--draft` writes a labelled preview instead.

steps.label: page opens: parseBundle(text)
steps.summary: The page reads its bundle back with `loadBundle`, and core's `parseBundle` checks the format and unpacks the index. A bundle that fails the check shows an error message instead of the guide.

steps.label: draw: deriveGraph(view, model)
steps.summary: `deriveGraph` combines the boxes of the view with the references in the index. Claude's text sits on top of the boxes and arrows that core works out.

frames.label: a rejected patch writes nothing: fix it, apply again

views.title: How the index finds the symbols in each file

scope.question: How does `xpl index` turn a repository into a symbol index?

steps.label: buildIndex({ root, precise, cache, commit })
steps.summary: The `xpl index` handler passes the root, the `--precise` mode, the cache setting and the commit to `buildIndex`, and with `--scip` the SCIP file to import. The result reports what the cache supplied apart from the work done fresh.

steps.label: detectGit(root, gitOptions)
steps.summary: `detectGit` finds the git work tree and the indexed root, and discovery reuses that answer. `xpl pr` runs this lookup in the repository it prepared, with a cleaned environment.

steps.label: discoverFiles(root, { git, languages, gitOptions })
steps.summary: `discoverFiles` keeps the source files of the selected languages and counts the files it leaves out, by reason, with up to three paths each. Files that git ignores and skipped folders are not counted.

steps.label: TreeSitterProvider.analyze(input)
steps.summary: The builder reads the current text of each file. The syntax provider reuses the cached facts of an unchanged file, or extracts them again, and records which it did.

steps.label: hashFile()
steps.summary: `hashFile` hashes a file with indentation and blank lines kept. The native hasher follows the versioned hash rules of core.

steps.label: pack.extract(ctx)
steps.summary: On a cache miss, the language pack parses the file and returns plain facts and diagnostics, and the adapter then frees the parse tree. A cache hit skips this step.

steps.label: normalizeProvider(input, output)
steps.summary: `normalizeProvider` checks the hashes and ranges that a provider reports, then `assembleSymbols` gives each symbol its id. Two symbols with the same path get numbers in source order.

steps.label: hashRange(range)
steps.summary: `hashRange` hashes all the source lines of each symbol. A change in whitespace therefore changes the hash, and the code links on that symbol drift.

frames.label: for each discovered file, in path order
the file's language has a pack

views.title: How the index finds references and saves itself

scope.question: How does `xpl index` turn a repository into a symbol index?

steps.label: resolveHeuristic(resolverInput)
steps.summary: The heuristic resolver matches every reference by scopes, imports and declared receiver types, also for files read from the cache. Go type inference runs again too, and a function used as a value stays a read.

steps.label: pack.resolveModule(spec, file, repo)
steps.summary: The pack of the importing file turns a module path into a file of the repository. The resolver then follows bindings and re-exports across those files.

steps.label: provider.analyze(input)
steps.summary: Syntax providers always run and may reuse the cached facts of a file. Semantic providers follow the `--precise` mode, run again on every build and return plain facts with a report of what they covered.

steps.label: ProviderOutput
steps.summary: The provider returns symbol identities, source text, references and coverage, and shared normalization checks them before the merge. Kinds that the provider does not support or did not examine keep their earlier heuristic references.

steps.label: normalizeProvider and mergeProvider
steps.summary: xpl checks positions and source text, then replaces only the reference kinds and files that the provider covered. Other references keep their `heuristic` label, and the bundle keeps the provider versions and labels.

steps.label: warn and keep heuristic references (or throw)
steps.summary: In `auto` mode a failed semantic provider prints a warning and the heuristic references stay, and in `require` mode the build fails. A failed syntax provider keeps the facts it checked before and reports its limits.

steps.label: resolveCommitId({ commit, git, files, root, gitOptions })
steps.summary: `resolveCommitId` names the index by the `--commit` label, the short HEAD of a clean tree, or a hash of the files. The index file takes that name.

steps.label: { index, warnings, exclusions, extraction, work }
steps.summary: `buildIndex` returns the index with the warnings, the files it left out and the timings. Only the symbols, references, hashes and coverage go into the saved index.

steps.label: writeIndex(root, index)
steps.summary: `writeIndex` writes a temporary file and renames it, so a reader never sees half an index. Index files and cache entries do not count as source, so they leave the commit id alone.

frames.label: --precise is not off: each resolver whose languages still have heuristic references
the tool described some files
else: the tool failed or described no file

views.title: How xpl apply checks and saves a patch

scope.question: How does a patch become validated, hash-checked anchors, and what happens when it is rejected?

steps.label: applyPatch(explainer, patch, model, texts, {actor})
steps.summary: `applyCommand.run` reads the patch, takes a file lock, loads the latest explainer and calls `applyPatch` while it holds the lock. `applyPatch` works on clones, so a failed patch leaves the caller's explainer as it was.

steps.label: upsertElement / upsertView / upsertTour
steps.summary: `run` merges nodes, edges, concepts, views and tours into the working copy, then `title`, `scope` and `remove`. For Claude's patch it skips each item the user wrote, and `validate()` runs even after a failed merge.

steps.label: mergeExisting(...) / convertFields(...)
steps.summary: `convertFields` turns each sent field into its stored form, and `mergeExisting` replaces those fields on a copy. For Claude's patch, a field the user edited keeps its value.

steps.label: makeAnchor(input, index, texts, options)
steps.summary: `makeAnchor` looks up the file and symbol of each code link in the patch and checks the input. For a name it cannot find, it suggests close names before any hashing.

steps.label: locateText(lines, find)
steps.summary: `locateText` turns a unique `find` text into a span of lines. Empty, missing or repeated text fails, and the message says where to look.

steps.label: hashOf(lines, range)
steps.summary: `hashOf` hashes the current lines of the span with the versioned hash rule. For a link on a whole symbol or file, `makeAnchor` also checks that the index matches the current text.

steps.label: {ok: true, anchor} | {ok: false, error}
steps.summary: `makeAnchor` returns the stored code link with its hash and range, or an error. `Applier` records an error on its patch path and goes on with the other checks.

steps.label: applyIncludeOps / applyStepUpdates
steps.summary: `applyIncludeOps` adds and removes the boxes of a map, and `applyStepUpdates` merges steps by id. Lists the user edited stay as they are.

steps.label: validateExplainer(input | work, index, texts, {mode: "strict"})
steps.summary: `validate()` checks the explainer before and after the merge. Elements that already failed are left out, so one bad input gives one error.

steps.label: resolveWith(anchor, index, texts)
steps.summary: `resolveWith` compares the stored hash with the current code. A changed or missing link becomes an error that says how to repair it.

steps.label: Issue[]
steps.summary: Errors that the patch adds, or that sit on elements it touches, reject the patch. Older errors elsewhere become warnings, so a small repair can still go in.

steps.label: ApplyResult {ok, explainer, issues, changed}
steps.summary: When an error is left, `fail()` returns the caller's own explainer, which no step changed, with `ok: false`. Otherwise the result holds the working copy, the warnings and the ids that changed.

steps.label: atomicWrite(path, jsonFile(result.explainer))
steps.summary: `atomicWrite` saves the accepted explainer, unless the run has `--dry-run`. The write ends before the command reports success.

steps.label: rejected: N errors, nothing was applied
steps.summary: `applyCommand.run` exits 1 for a rejected patch, or for one the user's edits block entirely, and writes nothing. The messages name each problem the author must fix.

for each AnchorInput
result ok, not --dry-run, something changed: write
else: rejected, or everything was user-protected (exit 1)

steps.summary: `layeredLayout` lays out the inside of each container first, then places the container as one box of the level above. Boxes the user pinned keep their place, and dagre places the rest.

scope.question: How does a click on a diagram element show its code in the editor?

steps.label: click(id, additive)
steps.summary: A click on a box, an arrow or a step selects it in the store. A click with a modifier key adds to the selection or takes away from it.

steps.label: set() calls the subscribers
steps.summary: `select()` ends in `set()`, which replaces the state with a copy and calls each subscriber. Components that read the state, such as `EditorStack` and `DiagramPane`, then render again.

steps.label: useDerived()
steps.summary: `useDerived` reuses the diagram, focus and match results whose inputs did not change. The code panes update when the selection changes.

steps.label: stubFocus(stub, vd, model)
steps.summary: Selecting an arrow to a box outside this map highlights the references it stands for and the code they point at. One such box can stand for several targets.

steps.label: codeFocus([id], model, { derivedEdges })
steps.summary: `codeFocus` turns the selected ids into ordered code ranges. For a derived arrow, the ranges come from the graph on screen.

steps.label: anchorRanges(anchors, owner, model)
steps.summary: `anchorRanges` turns each resolved code link into a range with its role and status. A missing link adds no range.

steps.label: nodeFocus(...) / derivedFocus(...)
steps.summary: Without code links, the focus follows the code itself: a symbol's lines, a file's text or a group's members. A derived arrow shows its reference sites and the definitions they point at.

steps.label: mergeFocusByFile(focus)
steps.summary: `mergeFocusByFile` groups the ranges by file and joins ranges that share a line into runs of whole lines. Each run keeps the roles of its ranges, so a call inside a definition stays visible.

steps.summary: `derivePanes` gives panes to the opened and primary files first, then to the other focused files. The files that do not fit are listed, and a "before" code link gets a pane of its own.

steps.summary: `EditorStack` draws one `EditorPane` per pane, and lists the files that did not fit with a button for each. In Present mode, `talkPanes` gives far-apart places of one file a pane each.

steps.label: applyFocus(editor, { ranges, dim })
steps.summary: `applyFocus` highlights the linked ranges and, when asked, dims the code around them. A drifted range gets a mark of its own.

steps.label: scrollToLine(editor, firstFocusLine)
steps.summary: `scrollToLine` scrolls the pane to its first focused range. Lines removed above a change stay in view, so you can compare.

steps.summary: CodeMirror's update listener runs when the selection changes or the editor gets focus, and turns the selection into line numbers. The listener then calls `handlers.onCursor`, the function that `EditorPane` gave to `createReadOnlyEditor`.

steps.summary: `viewReverseIndex` splits the candidates into drawn elements and concepts, and builds one reverse index for each group. `buildReverseIndex` files the code ranges of each candidate under their file and takes the derived arrows of the view as given.

views.title: Who uses xpl, and what it reads and writes

scope.question: What is xpl for, and who uses it?

tours.title: How xpl keeps a guide tied to its code

steps.note:
### xpl checks what Claude says about your code

You ask a question, and Claude reads your repository and writes the guide. xpl checks each code link against the code, saves the guide files and builds the page that your browser shows. You still check that the text is true.

### Claude works through the skill and the CLI

Claude starts from a draft: the CLI builds the boxes and steps from the code, and Claude fills in the text. `xpl apply` saves a patch from Claude only when its code links resolve.

### The index lists the code a claim may point at

The indexer reads each source file and records every function, class and config key with its lines and a hash. The later checks compare each claim with this index.

### One set of rules serves the CLI and the page

Core holds the guide format, the code links, the patch merge and the checks. Core reads no files, so the CLI and the page in your browser run the same rules.

### Four commands take a question to a page

The commands run in this order: index the code, start an empty guide, apply each patch, then bundle the page. The browser then draws each diagram from the index inside the page.

### Each code link stores a hash of its lines

`makeAnchor` finds the lines of a code link and stores their hash with indentation kept. A later whitespace change therefore also counts as a change, and the link drifts.

### A click lights up the code behind a box

A click on a box, an arrow or a step selects it, and `codeFocus` turns its code links into highlighted lines. A box without code links shows its own code: a function its lines, a file the whole file.

### When the code changes, xpl sorts each link

`xpl resolve` checks each code link again. A link is moved when its text is still in the symbol, drifted when the text changed and missing when the symbol is gone. Claude explains only the drifted parts again.

### Where to read next

The Viewer box opens the click path in detail. The detailed tour follows the index, the patch merge, the drawn arrows and the cursor lookup, and shows how your edits survive a new explanation.

tours.summary: xpl makes a guide to your code: diagrams next to the code, linked both ways. Claude writes the text, and xpl checks that each code link points at code that exists now. When the code changes later, xpl marks each link whose code changed, so Claude explains that part again. The result is one HTML file that opens without a server.

tours.title: In detail: the index, the patch merge and the page

steps.note:
### Four packages split the work

The CLI owns the files and the commands, the indexer reads code and the viewer draws the page. Core sits under these three, and each highlighted line imports it. The skill only runs the CLI.

### Language packs report facts, and the framework names them

Each language pack parses its files and reports plain facts: names, lines and references. The pack assigns no ids or hashes, and `assembleSymbols` names each symbol by its file and path and hashes its lines.

### Precise references replace heuristic ones file by file

A SCIP tool that skipped some files still makes the references of the other files precise. The skipped files keep their heuristic references, and the index counts those files in `heuristicFiles`.

### A patch replaces only the fields it sends

`mergeExisting` copies the element and replaces each sent field whole, so a sent list of members or steps replaces the old list. To add one member, Claude sends the whole list again.

### A rejected patch changes nothing on disk

Core merges the patch into a copy, and `fail()` hands back the original. Claude can therefore fix the listed problems in one pass and send the same patch again.

### Arrows between boxes are worked out, not stored

`deriveGraph` counts the references between two shown boxes and draws one arrow for them. A reference to code that the map does not show becomes a short arrow to a box outside this map, unless the map hides those.

### The cursor lights up the smallest matching box

For each line under the cursor, `lookup` returns the diagram parts with the smallest range around that line. A step's call therefore wins over the file around it, and a concept card can light up too.

### Line offsets count from the symbol's first line

Code added above a symbol moves only its first line, so its code links are moved without a search. Lines added inside the symbol shift the text, and `searchSpan` looks for that text within the symbol.

### A new explanation keeps what you wrote

You can correct a summary in the viewer and keep the correction. When Claude explains that part again after a code change, `convertFields` leaves each field you edited as you left it.

tours.summary: This tour goes one level below the main tour, for people who work on xpl. The index gets its symbols from language packs, and its references from SCIP tools where they run. A patch replaces only the fields it sends, and keeps the fields the user edited. The page works out its arrows and its cursor matches from the index each time.

scope.audience: Overview, then a deep dive, for people who use or work on xpl
